name: [R21] Unprivileged process suddenly transitions to root without a known escalation path (Infinity Core kernel LPE pattern)
message:
Exploratory heuristic for "Infinity Core": six Linux kernel local privilege-escalation bugs (timer, signal, memory management, futex, scheduler, SLUB/SLAB) disclosed 2026-10-16 by researcher Hyunwoo Kim (V4bel), with public exploit code (github.com/V4bel/InfinityCore). Five of six grant root to an unprivileged local user; CVE-2026-98260 (timer use-after-free in exec(), CVSS 7.8) is the primary one. No workaround exists -- kernel update + reboot only.

A kernel exploit leaves no reliable userspace log signature, so this is indirect: a process whose effective UID becomes 0 with no legitimate path (no sudo/su/sshd/login/systemd/cron/container-runtime binary, and the parent isn't already root). This shape is consistent with any local kernel exploit, not proof of Infinity Core specifically.

Confirm: check the host's kernel version with scripts/linux_kernel_infinitycore_check.py and the distro's own advisory before attributing a hit to these CVEs. Tune the allowlist of legitimate root-granting binaries to your own environment before trusting this rule -- the default list is a starting point, not exhaustive.

queries.name: unexplained_root_transition
queries.query: source:process_creation @process.new_uid:0 -@process.parent.user:root -@process.executable.path:(*\/sudo OR *\/su OR *\/sshd OR *\/login OR *\/systemd OR *\/cron OR *\/crond OR *\/containerd-shim OR *\/runc)
